audit.why: The lane is level 1 yours, 2-3 his as Leap Strike and Counter Strike come up, even at 4-5, yours at 6, then trending his with items.
audit.corrected: Rating kept; the stage story restored in the chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows disagreed with the packet while the whys under them were already right.
audit.why: whys[1] and whys[2] hand levels 2 and 3 to Jax, whys[4] hands level 6 to Olaf, whys[5] and whys[6] call the item stages coin-flips — the packet chart says exactly that, and the mirror reports flipping the same six rows.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 flipped as one atomic group across both layers, with ratings 6/4/4 on the first three.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings say Ragnarok 'cleanses' or 'strips' the Counter Strike stun.
audit.why: Riot's text gives passive armour and magic resist plus immunity to disables for as long as he keeps attacking — it prevents while active, it does not remove one already applied. The mirror flagged the same claim and left it; here it is rewritten to what the text does support.
audit.corrected: Restated as resists plus disable immunity while swinging, in whys[4], spikes[2], mid and wants.you[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings give Olaf's W sustain or omnivamp.
audit.why: Tough It Out is attack speed plus a shield; the lifesteal is the passive and grows as his health drops, which is exactly why a baited Counter Strike turns into a won grind rather than a won burst.
audit.corrected: Shield and lifesteal split in tradeGood, dosFull[1].d, whys[3] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is called matchup-defining without its cooldown.
audit.why: 17/15/13/11/9s — the longest cooldown in his laning kit by far, against Leap Strike's 8s and Empower's 7s falling to 3s. It is the only one worth waiting out.
audit.corrected: 17s written into breakdown.early, whys[3] and mid.

edits.before: Axe-slow + W sustain wins the first trades. Identify how Jax contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Undertow's slow into autos wins first contact — at level 1 Jax has neither Leap Strike nor Counter Strike.

edits.before: Axe-slow + W sustain wins the first trades. Respect Jax's Counter Strike completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.
edits.after: Undertow's slow and Tough It Out's shield win the first trades. From level 2 respect Counter Strike — its 17s is the number that decides every trade in this lane.

edits.before: Land the axe slow on Jax, walk the pickup for the reset, reave the true damage, and W-sustain whatever he answers with.
edits.after: Undertow him as he steps up, walk the pickup to reset its 9s, then Reckless Swing — Tough It Out shields his answer.

edits.before: Land the axe slow on Jax, walk the pickup for the reset, reave the true damage, and W-sustain whatever he answers with.
edits.after: Undertow him as he steps up, walk the pickup to reset its 9s, then Reckless Swing — Tough It Out shields his answer.

edits.before: Genuinely even — it becomes a pure E-timing duel: bait his Counter Strike and your W-omnivamp wins, eat it and you lose, skill decides.
edits.after: Genuinely even — a pure Counter Strike timing duel: bait its 17s and your missing-health lifesteal wins the grind, eat the stun and you lose.

edits.before: Ragnarok cleanses his E stun and grants armor/MR, so you dive through his combo and stick Q-slows — your strongest all-in window.
edits.after: Ragnarok's passive resists plus disable immunity while you swing let you dive his combo and stick the slow — your strongest window.

edits.before: Ragnarok cleanses his E stun and grants armor/MR — your hardest all-in window, dive him before his items land.
edits.after: Ragnarok gives passive resists and disable immunity while you keep swinging — dive him now, before his items land.

edits.before: All-in at 6 when Ragnarok cleanses his E stun and lets you stick with the Q-slow
edits.after: All-in at 6: keep swinging under Ragnarok so his stun never lands, and slow him

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a knife-fight: respect his E timer above all else — bait it out by faking the all-in, then E-Q-W once it's on cooldown and your omnivamp out-sustains the trade. Six is your spike: Ragnarok strips his E stun off you and gives armor/MR, so you can dive through his combo and stick him with Q-slows while your passive attack speed is ramping. This is the window to take plates or kill — his Trinity Force isn't online yet, so force the all-in now.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a knife-fight: respect Counter Strike's 17s above all else — bait it by faking the all-in, then commit once it is down and your missing-health lifesteal out-grinds him. Six is your spike: Ragnarok's resists plus disable immunity while you keep attacking let you dive through his combo and stick him with Undertow while your attack speed ramps. This is the window for plates or a kill — his Trinity Force isn't online yet.

notes: Chart was inverted on six of seven rows against its own whys — the page said Olaf wins levels 2 and 3 in the chart and Jax wins them in the text. Flipped to the packet, which the mirror also used. Ragnarok's 'cleanse' language removed in four places; the ability prevents disables while he keeps attacking and does not strip one already landed, so a Counter Strike stun that lands BEFORE you press R is not undone by pressing it. Jax's R is never named in this entry, which is just as well — the packet calls it Grandmaster-at-Arms while the mirror corrected it to Grandmaster's Might; worth settling centrally before anyone writes it here.
